newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen top-heavy in Asia, may test 115 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen top-heavy in Asia, may test 115 yen.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be top-heavy and range-bound during Asian trading time on Monday, although a test of the downside at 115 yen is possible, particularly if figures due out at 2350 GMT show a sharp rise in Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus.

Potential exporter sales and the chance of continued hedge selling from institutional investors expected to keep the topside heavy from 116 yen up, although the chance of rises on stop-loss buying exists should the greenback break above this level. A slide below last week's low of 114.70 yen could lead to sharp falls, but dealers were unsure how likely this was.

The dollar dipped to around 114.80 yen in Friday New York trade before recovering, largely on unconfirmed market rumours of dollar-buying intervention by a European central bank on behalf of the Bank of Japan (BOJ).
New York dealers had played down these rumours, but some Tokyo dealers said they thought such moves were indeed possible.
"When the dollar fell below 115 yen, the speed of its recovery was quite fast and seemed slightly abnormal, suggesting that perhaps these rumours were true," one trust bank dealer said.
